title: The “anti-social century” with Derek Thompson
author: Matthew Yglesias
text: Playback speed×SubtitlesShare postShare post at current time0:00/Paid episodeThe full episode is only available to paid subscribers of Slow Boring The “anti-social century” with Derek ThompsonWhat happens as people spend more and more time alone?Matthew YglesiasAug 27, 2026∙ PaidDerek Thompson coined the phrase “the anti-social century” to describe an incredible rise over the course of the 21st century in the amount of time that people spend alone. He recently joined Jerusalem and me to talk about it.This is an issue I’m concerned about. Recent technological progress has been very concentrated in the realm of home entertainment pursuits that have left people spending more time alone and lacking human connection.Jerusalem is more optimistic — insisting that we distinguish between loneliness and aloneness and that we see much clearer evidence of a rise in the latter than in the former. There’s nothing wrong, she argues, with people being alone as long as it’s not making them lonely and sad. It seems to me, though, that people increasingly are sad and angry even if they don’t say that they are lonely. And people who espouse moderate or liberal politics need some explanation for bad vibes that doesn’t cede the substantive ground to illiberal forces.
